keyFindings.text: **P3 | in window (`3aab896957e`) | A relayout backup has no restore command.** The run writes `<overlay folder>/relayout-runs/<stamp>/` and prints only `backup <label>` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:8879]. On success it then prints `<n> moved` and a bare `run ... apply` line [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:8939]. The engine has no command that reads that backup. `COMMAND_WORDS` holds only `status`, `apply`, `repin` and `pre-commit` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:123], and `--rollback` belongs to `repin` and reads only `repin-runs/<id>/backup.json` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:7409]. The relayout backup holds no `backup.json`, only copied sources and the manifest [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:8858]. Undoing a finished relayout that the operator regrets is therefore manual: copy the sources back, restore the manifest, and re-point each `relinked` layout link. Neither the engine nor the presentation contract names those steps. The contract shows only `Backup: [overlay folder]/relayout-runs/[stamp]/` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-overlay-presentation.txt:305]. The automatic undo (`rollbackRelayout`) runs only inside a failed run [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:8753]. Confirmed by reading. Not tested: whether the backup's layout is enough for a hand restore when the overlay folder sits outside the tree, where it is keyed from the overlay root [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:8849].

keyFindings.text: **P3 (UX, doc drift): the research `--extend` re-stop warning goes silent once the inbox has ever held a line.**

`extendResearch` counts every non-empty line of `research/inbox.jsonl` as a pending question [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/workflow-steps.cjs:195]. It shows the warning only when that count is zero [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/workflow-steps.cjs:206], and the warning text says "has no pending inbox question" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/workflow-steps.cjs:207].
Introduced by `2c80c64f391` (2026-11-17, inside the window: v4.1.0.0 is its ancestor). Moved into the script unchanged by `d239dd6d2ae`.

Nothing ever removes a consumed line. The reducer only reads the inbox [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:3431] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:3454]. It merges each line into the registry by `inboxId` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:1163]. The only other writers append [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:871] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:638].
Reproduced: a `complete` config with 3 iteration rows and one stale inbox line returned `"warning":null`. The same config with no inbox file returned the warning. Both runs exited 0.
So a question the run already answered still counts as pending, and the operator gets no warning before an extension that re-stops on `all_questions_answered` at once.

The fix is to count only inbox ids that the registry does not yet hold as answered, or to word the warning on coverage instead of the inbox [INFERENCE: based on the reducer's inboxId merge at reduce-state.cjs:1278 and the warning gate at workflow-steps.cjs:206].

The flag table tells operators to "add questions to `research/inbox.jsonl` before you extend" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/research.md:118]. It does not say that old lines already silence the warning.
Under `depth_mode == expansive` the inbox always holds the frontier rows [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:800], so the warning can never fire for that whole class of run.

keyFindings.text: **P3 (in window, `73d98332fff` with `777feef2920`): in degraded mode, a refused deep-loop command is printed as the reader's own choice.** The fallback keeps a `/deep:review` row whenever the command is typed and marks it `typed` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:4624]. It reads no refusal, by design [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/feature-catalog/python-compat/cli-shim.md:33]. Reproduced: `skill_advisor.py --force-local "please do not run /deep:review, just review the parser once"` returns `deep-review` at 0.95 with `"typed": true`. The CLI degraded path turns a typed tracked entry into a command recommendation with `typed: true` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:1563]. The renderer treats a `typed` deep-loop row as "the reader's own choice" and drops the A/B/C offer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:250]. So the brief prints `system-deep-loop → /deep:review (ask)` for a prompt that refused it. The native path withholds the command on the same prompt, so this is a parity gap the shim doc frames as harmless ("an `ask` the reader can decline"), while the renderer presents the command as a choice already made. The fallback-to-brief chain is inferred from code. The Python output is reproduced, but the degraded CLI path was not forced, because it needs an unreachable daemon. Policy stays `ask`, which limits the impact.

**P2 (`d57563b175a`): the one-packet check reads a packet path that ends at a JSON escape in the transcript wrong, so answers can land in the parent phase or in the only other packet named.** The transcript is JSONL, so a newline after a path is stored as the two characters `
`. The path regex stops only at whitespace and quotes [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:49], so the match keeps the trailing `
`. The leaf segment then fails `^\d{2,3}(?:--|-)[\w-]+$` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:52], and the normalizer breaks at it, keeping the segments before it [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:881]. The auto-record trim strips `.,;:!?)]}>` but not a backslash [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:831]. Reproduced on the compiled detector: a transcript line `A) specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/decision-capture/001-decision-capture/016-stop-hook-auto-record
proceeding` resolves to the parent `.../001-decision-capture`, which has a `spec.md`, so the `no_spec` guard does not catch it [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:205]. A top-level packet ending the same way drops out entirely. A transcript naming this packet and `specs/mcp/mcp-tooling/001-foo
` reports one packet, not two, which defeats the comment's stated intent that "a second packet named that way still counts against the one-packet rule" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:808]. The auto-record path shares the normalizer and the trim does not touch `\`, so it gives the same result. That part is [INFERENCE: based on the shared code at session-stop.ts:829-835 and the compiled run], because `autoRecordDecisions` itself was not run (it writes consumed keys into the real state directory). The normalizer predates the window and the autosave retarget has the same flaw. The in-window change is that a decision write now depends on it.

keyFindings.text: **P2, inferred, not reproduced (`d57563b175a`): Stop's auto-record races a concurrent save on the same packet, and the answers that lose the race are still marked consumed.** `writeDecisionRecord` reads the record [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/decision-record-writer.ts:787], rebuilds it in memory and writes it with temp-file-then-rename [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/decision-record-writer.ts:533] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/decision-record-writer.ts:819], with no lock. The writer has no lock anywhere. The Stop hook then appends the consumed keys [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:215] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-stop.ts:216]. The save workflow does the same sequence [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/core/workflow.ts:795] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/core/workflow.ts:805]. Suppose a second session's Stop or save writes the same `decision-record.md` between one writer's read and its rename. The rename then drops the other writer's rows, while both writers append their keys to the consumed log. The dropped answers are then never offered again by the nudge or a later save. This is a lost-update window, not a confirmed occurrence. Stop runs at every turn end, which makes it wider than it was when only explicit saves wrote. To confirm, run two writers in a loop against one scratch folder and check whether every consumed key's id is still in the record.
